correctness.rationale: For squarefree \(n\), the Euler product factorization is exact. The tail terms satisfy \(a_p\le\sum_{q>p}a_q\): eight initial primes have exact rational certificates, and for \(p\ge31\) Rosser–Schoenfeld supplies at least six primes in \((p,2p]\), whose logarithmic terms sum to more than \(p^{-2}>\log(1+p^{-2})\). The subsum lemma then fills the entire logarithmic tail interval. Scaling by the four choices at primes \(2\) and \(3\) gives the stated endpoints, and \(\pi>3.14\) separates the intervals.

value.rationale: This gives an exact component count and all endpoints for a natural squarefree divisor-function range, answering one concrete instance of the explicit gap-count question posed in Defant’s restricted-domain paper. The proof resolves an infinite tail analytically and provides exact rational boundary checks; it is not a finite enumeration or a routine restatement of the density threshold.
